jobs.title: Brand Manager - Sweaty Betty - 9M FTC
jobs.description:
We burst onto the scene as the OGs of female-first activewear back in 1998. And since then, we’ve been on a global mission to empower women through fitness and beyond. By uniting a global community of women – our sisterhood – together we encourage one another to embrace our bodies and everything we can do with them.
  
  
Our sisterhood treats every day like it’s made for moving, and we’re always pushing to do better too. Like using responsibly sourced materials, launching our first-ever FemTech collection – designed to keep you moving through menstruation, maternity and menopause – and supporting girls from all backgrounds to get into sport through our Sweaty Betty Foundation.
  
  
This is an exciting opportunity to join us as a Brand Manager as we continue our mission to empower women through fitness and beyond. You in?
  
  
**Our Values**
WE REALLY CARE ∙ FIRST, BEST, BRAVEST ∙ OUR STRENGTH IS IN EACH OTHER ∙ STAND UP, SPEAK UP, SHOUT OUT.
  
  
As Brand Marketing Manager, you will help deliver Sweaty Betty’s global brand strategy across core markets. You will develop and execute integrated campaigns and brand initiatives that build cultural relevance, brand consideration and business growth. The role requires a strong understanding of our consumer, social media, the cultural landscape and our commercial priorities, translating these into distinctive ideas and consistent execution across every customer touchpoint.
  
  
You will manage campaigns from strategy and briefing through to activation and measurement, working closely with Creative, Product, Growth, eCommerce, Social, PR, CRM, Retail, Wholesale and global market teams. You will ensure the work is insight-led, unmistakably Sweaty Betty and aligned to our female-first, rebellious and fearlessly stylish brand positioning.
  
  
**About The Role**

* Develop and execute full-funnel, 360° brand campaigns and global initiatives that drive brand and business results
* Own campaigns end to end, including strategy, insight, briefing, planning, creative development, production, activation, budget management and measurement
* Support the Senior Brand Manager in developing and executing Seasonal Brand Plans across the business.
* Own the organic social media strategy & calender for Sweaty Betty (predominately Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok & Strava) ensuring we are in her pathway and speaking to her in and unmistakably SB way with the most culturally relevant content. With the support of a Social Media Specialist.
* Ensure the timely delivery of marketing activity from creation through to execution, maintaining clear plans, responsibilities, approvals and critical paths.
* Be an expert on our consumer, category and cultural landscape, using insight to create relevant stories grounded in our brand truths.
* Turn Sweaty Betty’s brand strategy into distinctive campaigns, content and cultural moments that build consideration, conversation and demand.
* Create clear product stories within campaigns, connecting performance, style and consumer benefit while building fame for our icon products.
* Work closely with internal and external creative partners to develop the right idea and content for each channel, while maintaining one consistent brand story.
* Build joined-up brand experiences across owned, earned and paid touchpoints, turning audiences into brand and product fans.
* Partner with Growth and eCommerce teams to amplify key content and moments, support the customer journey and optimise activity through the funnel.
* Develop campaign objectives, metrics and measurement plans. Use brand and commercial results to assess effectiveness and improve future activity.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Campaigns are strategically clear, entertaining and unmistakably Sweaty Betty.
* Brand activity supports growth in consideration, cultural relevance, product demand and commercial performance.
* Campaigns land on time and on budget, with clear ownership and strong cross-functional alignment.
* Global consistency is balanced with relevant market adaptation.
* Performance is measured consistently and learning is applied to future plans.

**About You**

* Proven experience developing end-to-end marketing strategies and executing full-funnel, 360° campaigns within fashion, lifestyle, sport, fitness or a related industry.
* Strong strategic planning, campaign development and execution skills, with experience moving work from insight and idea through to launch and evaluation.
* A strong understanding of consumer behaviour, category dynamics and the cultural landscape, with the ability to turn insight into compelling brand stories.
* Excellent creative judgement and the confidence to challenge safe or generic work constructively.
* Commercial awareness and the ability to connect brand activity to consumer behaviour, product demand and business performance.
* Excellent collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with experience working across internal teams, global markets and external partners.
* Strong project-management skills, including experience managing budgets, agencies, production partners and competing priorities.
* Confident using metrics and results to evaluate activity, optimise performance and make recommendations.
* A self-starter who can move seamlessly from strategy into action and maintain momentum in a fast-moving environment.
* Clear, persuasive communication and presentation skills.
* People-management experience is desirable.

On an interim basis (until July 2027) this role will also be responsible for leading Sweaty Betty’s influencer programme as a maternity cover, overseeing the programme strategy, talent and agency relationships, campaign integration and delivery, with an influencer specialist as a direct report.

jobs.description:
**About Us**
The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.
  
  
At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.
  
  
In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.
  
  
Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.
  
  
Build a newsworthy career at the FT.
  
  
Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion
  
  
We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.
  
  
The Role
  
  
The Marketing Manager, B2B Lifecycle will own and develop defined areas of the B2B lifecycle strategy across FT Professional and the FT Specialist portfolio, with a primary focus on renewal and customer value growth through cross-sell and upsell.
  
  
You will own a portfolio of lifecycle programmes spanning renewal support, retention, cross-sell and upsell, delivering measurable improvements in account growth, renewal rates and customer lifetime value. The role will also flex across earlier lifecycle stages, including trial engagement, onboarding and in-life engagement, where required to support broader commercial priorities.
  
  
Working closely with the Head of B2B Lifecycle, you will translate the overall lifecycle strategy into quarterly plans, prioritised initiatives and commercial outcomes. Using customer insight and performance analysis, you will find opportunities, determine where resource should be focused and lead programmes designed to improve renewal outcomes and drive expansion within existing accounts.
  
  
You will work closely with collaborators across B2B Marketing, Sales, Data & Analytics and Marketing Automation to ensure lifecycle programmes support wider product, proposition and account strategies while remaining focused on customer outcomes. Marketing Automation will design and build campaigns and journeys from the briefs and strategic requirements you develop.
  
  
A core part of the role is ownership of business performance. You will define KPIs, monitor progress against commercial objectives, identify risks and opportunities, and recommend interventions that improve renewal performance, account growth and customer lifetime value.
  
  
As part of the Experience and Lifecycle Centre of Excellence, you will also help establish and embed consistent lifecycle frameworks, playbooks and ways of working across FT Professional, FT Specialist and Consumer Lifecycle.
  
  
Key responsibilities
  
  
**Lifecycle strategy and planning**

**We have momentum - Help create a cult brand.**

Slough | Hybrid: 1–2 office days a week

c. £55,000 + share options

**We've made it onto the shelves of thousands of stores, and into online marketplaces. Now help make Zombie a shopping-list obsession.**

We're Zombie. We make monstrously fruity snacks that kids love, and parents feel good about buying.

With growing distribution across Tesco and Sainsbury's, award-winning products, bold packaging and an awesome pipeline of new products, we've got serious momentum.

Now we want more people to discover us, try us, come back for more and tell their friends.

That's where you come in.

We're looking for a
**creative, social-first Marketing Manager**
who knows how to make a brand impossible to ignore. Someone who can come up with original ideas, create entertaining content, build a passionate community and turn that attention into genuine consumer demand.

Our ambition? To be a big player in the category. A brand that entertains, that people actively seek out, feel part of and enthusiastically recommend.

**Your mission: grow the Zombie uprising.**

* **Make us impossible to ignore.**
  Dream up and personally create original, funny, shareable content that brings Zombie's distinctive personality to life. Instagram will be your main playground, with parents and adult shoppers your primary audience.
* **Give people reasons to come back.**
  Build an engaged community of Zombie fans who love the brand, buy our products and spread the word. We're interested in genuine engagement and loyalty, not just follower counts.
* **Recruit the horde.**
  Find and develop relationships with creators, ambassadors and fans who can produce brilliant, authentic content and champion Zombie.
* **Turn attention into demand.**
  Use paid social to amplify great creative ideas, test different messages and content, and learn what drives awareness, trial and sales. You'll be confident managing Meta campaigns yourself.
* **Bring it all together.**
  Connect social, creators, paid advertising, consumer engagement and targeted activations into marketing that builds a distinctive brand and gets more Zombie products into shopping baskets.

You'll work closely with our founder, with real freedom to shape ideas and bring them to life. This is a hands-on role: you'll be creating content and delivering campaigns yourself, supported by specialist freelancers across design, influencers, gaming and web development.

**The brains we're looking for**

You're a creative, social-first marketer who knows how to make people stop scrolling, laugh, share and fall in love with a brand.

You can show us brilliant content you've personally created, including short-form video, and know how to use Meta advertising\* to amplify great ideas and deliver results.

You're hands-on, commercially curious and love turning ideas into action.

Challenger-brand experience will help. Food and drink, beauty, nutrition, pet care… we're open to different consumer categories and both DTC and omnichannel backgrounds.

Above all, bring humour, initiative and the energy to thrive in a small, ambitious team.

*\* We can build Meta skills if it’s a development need*

**The juicy bits**

Real ownership, creative freedom and agility. Plus share options, 24 days' holiday, company pension, bespoke marketing training and 10 working days a year to work from abroad.

**Ready to help build a brand people can't stop talking about?**

Apply through LinkedIn or contact Adrian Dalby at New Chapter Consulting with your CV and a short introduction.

New Chapter Consulting are our exclusive recruitment partners for this appointment. CVs sent directly to Zombie by recruiters will be redirected to Adrian Dalby at New Chapter Consulting.

jobs.description:
**Men are dying too young – and it doesn’t have to be that way.**
Around the world, men are facing a health crisis: prostate cancer, testicular cancer, poor mental health and suicide. At Movember we’re on a mission to change the face of men’s health by making it easier for men to talk, act and live longer healthier lives.
  
  
Every project, every campaign, every idea adds up to real change. You’ll be part of a purpose-fueled crew who believe making an impact and having fun should go hand in hand. Your mission is calling.
  
  
**DO GOOD. Work for Movember.**
**Your Mo-Mission (should You Choose To Accept It)**
Some of the most important partnerships Movember will ever build won’t be measured in dollars raised. They’ll be measured in credibility earned, policy shaped, and reach into the communities and institutions that determine how men’s health is understood, funded, and addressed.
  
  
As Strategic Impact Partnerships Manager, you’ll build and manage Movember’s portfolio of mission-aligned partnerships across the UK, working with research institutions, NGOs, sector bodies, professional associations, and advocacy organisations whose primary value to Movember is what they know, who they reach, or who they have the ear of. These are the partners who make Movember’s programs more credible, more scalable, and more influential, particularly with the organisations and individuals who shape government policy, public discourse, and sector practice around men’s health across suicide prevention, mental health, prostate cancer, and testicular cancer.
  
  
You’ll own the full partnership lifecycle from identification and proposition development through to activation, stewardship, and review. That means mapping the policy and influence environment, building compelling mutual value propositions, developing co-investment, grant, or in-kind contribution arrangements where appropriate, and maintaining the kind of trust-based relationships that deepen over time rather than plateau after the first year.
  
  
Critically, this role requires genuine commercial fluency alongside mission expertise. Strategic impact partners often represent latent opportunities to grow the Movember movement through fundraising activation, brand association, or income generation. Recognising those opportunities, knowing when and how to raise them, and doing so without compromising the mission relationship is a core part of the role.
  
  
You’ll work closely with Portfolio Leads, the Institute and Impact team, the Advocacy and Policy leads, and the Marketing and Communications team, acting as the connective tissue between external partners and the internal teams who can put their expertise, networks, and advocacy to work.
  
  
**No Moustache Required - But The Following Are**

* Deep understanding of the men’s health landscape, including the research, policy, advocacy, and sector bodies that shape it, with the ability to map and navigate the policy and influence environment to build credibility, access, and advocacy weight through strategic partnerships.
* Proven ability to develop and manage partnerships where the primary value exchange is mission-based rather than financial, and to articulate that value clearly to both internal and external stakeholders.
* Skilled at identifying and structuring partnerships with diverse organisations, from large research institutions to small specialist advocacy groups.
* A self-starter who proactively identifies and develops new opportunities rather than waiting for them to arrive.
* Ability to build trust and credibility quickly with senior stakeholders in academic, NGO, and sector body contexts, and to sustain those relationships over the long term.
* Understands when and how to introduce financial or in-kind elements into a mission partnership without distorting the relationship.
* Strategic thinker with the ability to assess the long-term positioning and credibility value of a potential partner, not just their immediate utility.
* Able to bring together communities of impact partners to work in coalition and align on joint goals.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including high-quality proposals, briefings, and partnership reviews, with the ability to translate complex impact and research information into compelling, accessible narratives.
* Proficiency with Salesforce or equivalent CRM tools for pipeline tracking and relationship management.

**Not Mission Critical - But For Extra Bonus Points**

* Knowledge of men’s health, specifically prostate cancer.

**Good Cause**
Working for Movember, you’ll help turn ideas (and moustaches) into millions for men’s health. Every bit we raise changes the face of men’s health by funding research, improving treatments, and supporting programs that help save lives.
  
  
We’re even shaping government policies on men’s health worldwide. By meeting directly with lawmakers, and helping them understand how more investment on men’s health benefits not just men, but all the communities they serve.
  
  
**Good Vibes**
We love weekends. That’s why our Fridays finish early for nine months of the year. But we also love our office vibe. Because here, it always feels like something big is about to happen. Be it an office-wide surprise birthday party (with cake!) or an open invite for all to hit the pub.
  
  
Come the hairy season, the energy cranks up. We’re talking celebrity visits. Live stunts on-site for TV and radio. And when we hit a fundraising milestone, the office gong might even go off. But, for those who prefer calm, no probs: hybrid working means you work where you feel best.
  
  
**Good Crew**
Spoiler alert: we’re a no-ego, all-impact crew. That means everyone gets a say, from new starters to those leading the charge. Collaboration over hierarchies, curiosity over rigid process. And it’s true across all our offices worldwide. We work as one, sharing expertise and celebrating wins. All in the name of making the biggest impact
